name: BLOCK DOMINOES WITH SPINNERS
description: Block Dominoes with Spinners is a variant of Block Dominoes where the first double played becomes a 'spinner' â€” tiles can be placed on all four sides of it, creating a cross-shaped layout with up to four open ends. This dramatically increases the number of playable positions compared to the two-end standard block game. The key question is whether ONLY the first double is a spinner, or ALL doubles are spinners.

This dramatically increases the number of playable positions compared to the two-end standard block game. The key question is whether ONLY the first double is a spinner, or ALL doubles are spinners.

A modification of standard Block Dominoes that adds the 'spinner' mechanic â€” allowing play on all four sides of a double. This creates the cross-shaped layouts familiar from many American domino games.
2 to 4 players. Partnership play possible with 4.
Double-six domino set (28 tiles). Can also use double-nine or double-twelve sets for more players.
Double-six domino set. Optional: Cribbage board for scoring.
2 players: 7 tiles each. 3 players: 5 tiles each. 4 players: 5 tiles each. Remaining tiles stay in the boneyard.

items.text: Single Spinner: Only the first double is a spinner. Other doubles are placed crosswise but not expanded. The more strategic variant.
All Spinners: Every double is a spinner â€” creates extremely branching layouts. Less strategic due to many open ends. Can require 'chicken foot' placement to fit on the table.
Dutch Variant (with Draw): When unable to play, draw 1-2 tiles from boneyard. Last two tiles remain undrawn. Double-zero counts as 13 pips.
Double-Nine Eight-Arm: With double-nine set, play starts on all four sides AND four corners of the spinner, giving 8 arms.
